fault: The {KEY} rattles when typed on because its stabilizer bar or stabilizer inserts are loose or dry.
diagnosis: A rattling space bar is almost always the stabilizer bar rubbing or clicking against its clips. I will take the keycap off, check that the bar is seated in its clips, clear any debris, and put the keycap back on evenly.
safety_notes: Unplug the USB-C cable before touching anything under the keycap.
Touch grounded metal first to discharge static before reaching into the board.
Lift the keycap evenly and do not force the stabilizer bar, because it can bend or snap.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal first to discharge static.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged into the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while working under the keycap.
Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.

steps.title: Remove the keycap
steps.instruction: Hook the keycap puller under both ends of the {KEY} keycap and lift evenly. Set the keycap aside.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is off and set aside, and the switch and stabilizer bar are visible.
common_mistakes: Lifting only one end, which bends the stabilizer bar.
Pulling at an angle, which stresses the switch stem or scratches the keycap.

steps.title: Check the stabilizer bar
steps.instruction: Look at the stabilizer bar under the {KEY}. Check that its ends are seated in both clips and that the bar is not bent.
steps.expected_visual_state: The stabilizer bar is visible, with both ends sitting in their clips and the bar straight.
common_mistakes: Not noticing that one end has popped out of its clip.
Bending the wire bar while checking it.

steps.title: Clean out debris
steps.instruction: Blow compressed air around the stabilizer and the {KEY} switch to clear dust and crumbs. Hold the can upright.
steps.expected_visual_state: The area around the stabilizer and switch is clear of dust and crumbs.
common_mistakes: Tilting the compressed air can, which sprays liquid.
Leaving crumbs trapped near the stabilizer clips.

steps.title: Put the keycap back
steps.instruction: Hook the {KEY} keycap onto the stabilizer ends first. Then press both ends down evenly until it seats.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap sits level at the same height as the surrounding keycaps.
common_mistakes: Pressing down only one end so the keycap sits crooked.
Not seating the keycap fully so it sits higher than the others.

steps.title: Reconnect and test
steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and press the {KEY} three times, including at both ends. Listen for the rattle.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged in, the backlight is on, and the {KEY} presses cleanly with no rattle.
common_mistakes: Testing only the middle of the key and not both ends.
Not checking that the key still registers once per press.
